title: Metric Blindspot Mitigation — proposal (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a proposal + quick runbook edits to reduce "metric blindspots" — classes of missing or malformed telemetry that cause noisy SLO-burn and derivative alerts (pager churn) and make triage slow. It's intentionally pragmatic: short-term mitigations on-call can apply, plus experiments to validate automated suppression and longer-term instrumentation fixes.

Background / motivation:
- Over the past 6 months we've noticed repeated noisy SLO-burn and derivative alerts tied to gaps in metric coverage rather than real service regressions. Example symptoms: sudden drop to zero in a request-per-second metric for a subset of instances, concurrent errors in the telemetry agent logs, and SLO% showing spiky burn despite client success rates being nominal.
- Root causes seen so far include: agent upgrades that renamed metrics, SDK sampler changes, histogram resets on process restarts, and an intermittent proxy that drops metric batches during GC windows.
- Current alerting rules are brittle: derivative thresholds (d/dt) fire on transient telemetry drops, and there is limited correlation between trace-level data and metric-level alerts because request_id isn't propagated into infra metrics.

Incident example (shortened):
- 2026-01-07 03:24 UTC: SLO-HighLatency service alerted (SLO burn = 18% in 5m)
- Investigations: request latency traces show tail latencies normal; infra request count metric for shard svc-x went to 0 at 03:22 and recovered at 03:30.
- Telemetry agent logs (container stdout) show: "metrics: dropping batch, http 502 upstream" correlating with a rolling restart of collector pod due to scheduled job.
- Conclusion: alert fired because the numerator/denominator used for SLO calc used missing denominator buckets; SLO math saw effective error rate spike. Pager noise for oncall was avoidable.

Key observations / heuristics:
- Missing or zeroed denominators are more dangerous than noisy numerators for SLOs — they produce false-positive burn alerts.
- Alerts triggered by derivative/delta rules are particularly susceptible to telemetry batch loss.
- Short-lived collector failures are common during infra deploys and GC windows; we don't have a synthetic heartbeat that validates the telemetry path end-to-end.

Immediate oncall runbook additions (to be merged into oncall playbook):
1) Quick triage: check telemetry-agent-logs for dropouts (collector, proxy, agent) and note agent versions.
2) Check "metric freshness" dashboard (panel: metric_health_overview -> freshness_by_service) for matching drops.
3) If denominator metrics are zeroed but traces show requests: mark as "telemetry outage suspected" and set alert to acknowledge and mute derivative alerts for 10 minutes for affected rule IDs (manual squelch).
4) Create temporary synthetic check: curl /health on a small canary instance and ensure that telemetry pipeline surfaces the canary metric in <60s; document result in incident notes.
5) Escalation: if collector component logs show 502/504 upstreams for >5m, escalate to infra-oncall and tag deploy owner.

Triage checklist (short form):
- Was there a deploy in the 30m window? Link to deploy job.
- Is telemetry-agent version different on affected hosts?
- Any histogram resets (process restarts) reported in metrics_exporter logs?
- Are there 5xx responses from telemetry forwarder/proxy (check Prometheus exporter, agent, gateway logs)?
- Cross-check traces for request_id presence and count parity with metrics.

Short-term mitigations / experiments (A/B):
A) Synthetic path freshness probe (canary metric)
- Deploy a lightweight synthetic traffic generator that emits tagged metrics every 30s and track end-to-end latency from generation -> ingestion -> dashboard. Alert only when synthetic path latency > 90s or missing for >2 consecutive intervals.
- Goal: distinguish telemetry outages vs real traffic drops.

B) Squelch-by-context (automatic suppression heuristic)
- Implement an experiment where derivative SLO alerts are suppressed if a telemetry-freshness probe for that service is failing. Use a 5m inhibition window.
- Monitor false-negatives carefully; start with non-critical SLOs.

C) Alert deduping via request_id correlation (PoC)
- Add an index by request_id on the metric ingestion pipeline for a subset of services. When an alert fires, attempt to correlate with recent traces sharing request_id to confirm real failures.
- If correlation not found, mark alert as "telemetry-likely" in UI (for human triage).

Long-term remediations (priority list):
1) Standardize agent metric names and enrich CI to fail builds when metric name changes are detected without a compat flag. (owner: infra/telemetry)
2) Instrument a minimal set of "denominator" metrics for all customer-facing routes and ensure request_id propagation through infra metrics. (owner: platform-engineering)
3) Implement per-service synthetic check pipeline with SLA for ingestion latency (<60s). (owner: observability)
4) Improve histogram persistence across restarts or store pre-restart snapshots to avoid zeroing buckets when process restarts. (owner: serving-runtime)
5) Add a telemetry-quality index to the Console so incidents can quickly surface whether an alert is likely a telemetry outage. (owner: console-and-tooling)

Metrics to track (for experiment and rollout):
- Synthetic-path missing rate (target <0.01 over 24h).
- Fraction of SLO alerts tagged as "telemetry-likely" (should drop as fixes roll out).
- Pager churn per week (pager opens / unique infra incidents), track 4-week moving average.
- Time-to-detect true user-impacting incidents vs false-positive alerts.

Rollout plan (90-day timeline):
- Week 0–2: Add oncall runbook edits + synthetic probe PoC on staging; smoke test.
- Week 3–6: Launch canary synthetic probes for 10% of services; start squelch-by-context experiment for non-critical SLOs.
- Week 7–12: Audit agent metric naming across services; CI checks and a migration window for renames.
- Week 13–90: Full rollout of synthetic probes, request_id correlation PoC -> production, dashboard and Console integration.

Open questions / risks:
- False suppression risk: could suppress real incidents if synthetic probe doesn't exercise the failed path. Mitigation: have multiple synthetics per critical flow and keep conservative thresholds.
- Cost / cardinality: adding request_id to metrics and indexing increases storage. Need a bounded retention and selective sampling.
- Ownership clarity: telemetry touches multiple teams; need a short RACI to avoid finger-pointing during incidents.

Action items / TODOs (assigned approximate owners):
- [Maya] Draft runbook PR for oncall playbook updates (due 2026-02-25).
- [Owen] Spin up synthetic probe PoC in staging + create Grafana panels (due 2026-03-05).
- [Lucia] Start agent-name audit across repositories, open compat flag RFC (due 2026-03-12).
- [Samir] Prototype request_id correlation PoC with 1 service (due 2026-03-20).
- [Evan] Cost estimate for indexing request_id samples (due 2026-03-10).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could consider a "telemetry second opinion" microservice that ingests a light-weight subset of events (synthetics + samples) and returns a health verdict API for suppression rules.
- Consider adding a metric "denominator-coverage_ratio" that reports how many routes have both numerator+denominator in current scrape window; use this to gate SLO alerts.

References and related tickets:
- SRE-4123: recent SLO noisy alerts post-collector-upgrade (linked above)
- telemetry PR #289: rename-protections for agent metrics (PoC)
- Slack thread: #sre-observability: "telemetry batch drops 2026-01-07" (linked above)

If you are reading this and have a strong objection to automatic squelch rules, add a comment below and ping @eng-sre — we will default to manual-squelch for the first 2 months.

End of draft.
summary: Proposal (WIP) describing short-term runbook edits, experiments, and long-term fixes to reduce noisy SLO alerts and pager churn caused by missing or malformed telemetry (metric blindspots).
